title: The Reservoir by Jake Brasch at Atlantic Theater Company #thereservoi...
transcript: The Reservoir is a quirky new play full of heart but not to the point of crumbling under the weight of its earnestness. When Josh returns home after a futile attempt to get sober, he finds himself dealing with brain fog and the aching feeling that life is passing him by. Reconnecting with all four of his grandparents, who are in varying stages of mental decline, gives him a renewed sense of urgency and meaning, but looking after them and himself is an uphill battle, to say the least. The writing feels natural and the performances, though a bit heightened for my usual taste, are nicely calibrated to the stylized way that the story is delivered. The scenes, of which there are many, transition seamlessly and the actors function as a sort of greek chorus when they aren't assuming their primary roles. To that point, everyone's busy but the narrative is clear. This production is excellently cast, featuring veterans like Chip Zien and Caroline Aaron who both develop their characters effortlessly, despite the fragmented nature of their presence in the play. Noah Galvin leads this play with an optimism and humor without undercutting the bleakness that's also a major element here. I felt spoiled having such close proximity to witness his microexpressions. He has these puppy-like eyes that contain so much depth, as if they themselves are a reservoir. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
